issues.description: Class 'Lecture' constructor parameter mismatch: the problem statement and UML require a constructor that initializes five attributes in this exact order: (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors). The template's Lecture.java currently provides a constructor with only three parameters (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents) at the signature on line 7, while the solution implements the five-parameter constructor on line 13. This inconsistency between the template and the specification will confuse students about the required constructor signature and can cause tests or example usage that expect the five-parameter constructor to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to match the UML and problem description: declare the five private attributes (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) and replace the current three-parameter constructor stub with the five-parameter constructor using the exact parameter order from the UML: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) { this.lectureName = lectureName; this.numberOfInscribedStudents = numberOfInscribedStudents; this.numberOfGuestStudents = numberOfGuestStudents; this.numberOfLecturers = numberOfLecturers; this.numberOfTutors = numberOfTutors; } Keep TODO comments only for genuinely incomplete pedagogical tasks, not for incorrect signatures.
